summary: Explains the file module `mode`: quote octal values for consistent results, since a leading zero sometimes fails in loops and bare numbers are read as decimal. Symbolic modes work since 1.8; without mode, new objects use umask and existing ones keep theirs. Also covers `modification_time`.
questions: Should I write mode as '0755' or 0755 in the file module?
Why do my permissions come out wrong inside a loop?
How do I set a file's modification time?
What mode does a new directory get if I don't set one?

answer_card.title: file mode and modification_time
answer_card.answer_md:
`mode` is octal. For consistent results **quote** it (`'644'`, `'1777'`). A leading zero (`0755`) works sometimes but can fail in loops and other cases. A bare number without either is read as decimal and gives unexpected results. Symbolic modes work since 1.8 (`u+rwx`, `u=rw,g=r,o=r`). Without `mode`, new objects use the system `umask` and existing ones keep their mode; set `mode` to be sure (CVE-2020-1736).

`modification_time` (2.7): `preserve`, `YYYYMMDDHHMM.SS`, or `now`; default `preserve` for `state=file/directory/link/hard` and `now` for `state=touch`.
